## Interpretation (discovery tier)

No singular Jacobian was found in any of the 8 tested configurations.
The discovery-tier evidence strongly supports the rank conjecture in
B2 proof.md §4, but does NOT constitute an analytic proof.

The analytic proof task is: show that for Li-type (or moment-type) tests,
the map t -> (A_{j,k}(t))_{j,k} is algebraically independent / has nonzero
Wronskian, so the Jacobian is generically full rank over Q.

## Next step (P3, Days 15-21)

Attempt a formal proof of generic full rank:
- For Li-type: use the fact that phi_j(1/2+it) are distinct analytic
  functions of t, and the Vandermonde-like structure.
- For moment-type: Re[(1/2+it)^{-k}] are real parts of powers; their
  Wronskian determinant is nonzero for distinct t values (Vandermonde-type
  argument in disguise).

If the analytic proof succeeds, B2-RANK-CONJECTURE is promoted to
PROOF-DRAFT and the full B2 construction can proceed.
